title: The UX checklist, version 1 — UXR-3, the look-and-feel review (docs/UX_UI_REVIEW_PLAN.md §UXR-3)
frozen: October 13, 2026, Pre-Deploy S11 Part 1, before the first reading. The rules are the S11 hand-off's 'Decided in advance' (docs/NEXT_SESSION_PROMPT.md), made under the user's October 13, 2026 delegation ('make all decisions … nothing hanging'). No edit after this commit: tests/test_uxr3_checklist_frozen.py pins the ids, the surface order and the SHA of the canonical JSON. A new version is a new file.
routing: docs/PRE_DEPLOY_PLAN.md §2: row S11 reads; row S12 ('UXR-3 fixes') fixes, worst surfaces first

kinds.instrument: read off the shoot's machine records by a tool, the same way every time
kinds.reader: three blind readers; the mark two of the three give (the user's marks at UXR-4, S15, override)
kinds.driven: a driven record: the action probe, the Mode C session, an existing driven test

items.name: Readable
items.text: 0 RED rows in UXR-0 at all five resolutions
items.instrument: tools/uxr0_readability_report.py (run with -X utf8) over the shoot's index.json
items.pass_rule: ✓ iff the surface has an ok reading (the harness's `ok`: no shot error, a non-blank frame) at each of the five resolutions and every reading counts 0 RED and 0 P1 rows by the instrument's own classify(): body-class text RED under 16 physical px em and P1 under 13; caption-class (Caption / CaptionRich / CaptionButton) RED under 14 and P1 under 12. The map's world-space tier is counted beside the floor (map_small) and never scored. A missing or failed reading at any resolution is ✗: it cannot be evidenced. Decided: §UXR-3 says four resolutions; the instrument reads five and the fifth is the user's own monitor, so the stricter reading holds.

items.name: Hierarchy
items.text: The one thing the surface is for is the largest or first element; the eye lands on it in the frame
items.pass_rule: Each of the three blind readers marks ✓ or ✗ from the surface's frames (the 1920×1080 frame and the user's 5120×1440 frame; any of the five may be opened). The surface's purpose is its name and its IQ-10 must_show line. ✓ iff that one thing is the largest or the first element and the eye lands on it. A reader who cannot judge from the evidence marks ✗ and says why. The item's mark is the one two of the three give.

items.name: Contrast
items.text: Body text ≥ 4.5:1 against its panel, captions ≥ 3:1 (measured off the frame)
items.instrument: tools/uxr2b_contrast_report.py (run with -X utf8) over the shoot's index.json, with High contrast OFF: the default a new player sees
items.pass_rule: ✓ iff the surface has an ok reading at each of the five resolutions, and each reading measures at least one text row and finds 0 rows under the floor: body-class ≥ 4.5 : 1, caption-class ≥ 3 : 1. The ratio is WCAG's, between the text's declared colours (font colour, BBCode spans and chip pairs, times the modulate chain) and the frame's median background under the row's rect. Disabled buttons, the disabled chip (Utils.bb_chip_disabled) and the map tier are not measured, as the instrument defines. A missing or failed reading is ✗. High contrast ON is shot and recorded beside it and never scores.

items.name: Consistency
items.text: Chrome, chips, close-X, headings and spacing match the theme (no one-off colours or sizes; the override census)
items.instrument: tools/uxr3_consistency_census.py (built in Part 2 to this rule) over the surface's own files
items.pass_rule: ✓ iff the census finds 0 hits in the surface's own files. A hit is one of two kinds. (a) A ONE-OFF SIZE: a raw font-size override as tests/test_uxr2_override_diet.py's raw_sites counts it (the RAW_RATCHET census: a scene's theme_override_font_sizes/* line; a script's add_theme_font_size_override( call, literal or computed; the set(...) and string-call dodges), or a BBCode [font_size= in script code. Each is a size outside the named theme steps, and a named exemption of that test still counts. (b) A ONE-OFF GREY: a colour in Utils.is_dim's class (chroma ≤ 0.12 and 0.15 ≤ luminance ≤ luminance(UI_TEXT_DIM) + 0.02, where luminance = 0.2126 r + 0.7152 g + 0.0722 b on the authored values) written as a literal and not routed through Utils.toned / toned_hex / the COLOR tokens. In script code (comments and docstrings dropped) that is a Color(r, g, b[, a]) of numeric literals, a Color("…") or Color.html("…") hex, a [color=…] hex, a bare 6- or 8-digit hex string literal, or a named Godot grey (Color.GRAY and kin), outside any toned( / toned_hex( call. In a scene it is a theme_override_colors/*, modulate or self_modulate value that is not a step of Utils.DIM_LADDER (±1/255 per channel): the High-contrast chokepoint raises a ladder value, so an off-ladder grey is a one-off. The surface's own files are the scene files and scripts (with their base scripts) of every node visible in its frames, plus the shot's own scene and root script. They never include scripts/utils.gd (the palette's home, where the tokens live), scripts/ui_settings.gd, the theme .tres, tools/** or the engine's built-ins. An unreachable surface's files are its scene, the scripts that scene attaches and their bases: the census needs no frame. A reader's 'looks inconsistent' note is recorded beside the mark and never fails the item without a census hit.

items.name: Affordance
items.text: Everything clickable looks clickable and everything that looks clickable is; disabled states say why (honest availability)
items.pass_rule: ✗ when the driven record (the action probe) finds a SILENT control: enabled, visible, pressed, and nothing at all happened. It looks clickable and is not. Otherwise each blind reader marks ✓ or ✗ from the frames and the probe's record of the surface's controls: every control, its class, whether it answered and how, and every disabled control with its tooltip and the text beside it. ✓ iff everything that is a control looks like one, nothing that looks clickable is inert, and every disabled control states why (its tooltip, a reason line beside it, or the chip's own reason). The reader mark is the one two of the three give. A surface the probe cannot reach is ✗: the driven half cannot be evidenced.

items.name: Feedback
items.text: Every action answers within the frame (a chip echoes, a send acknowledges, a save confirms)
items.pass_rule: ✓ iff the driven record shows every action of the surface answering within the frame. Every enabled control the action probe presses must answer VISIBLE: within 500 ms and 30 frames of the press something on screen changed (a visible text, a node shown or hidden, a control's rect, a button's pressed or disabled state, the focus owner, the map's camera), or the surface closed, or another surface opened. A HANDOFF control (its only answer an API call or an outward signal) counts as answering only where a live-backend driven record shows that road's visible answer: the Mode C session or an existing driven test, cited by name. A NOT PRESSED control (a scene change, quit, save, load, new game) counts only the same way. Unproven is ✗: a SILENT control, an uncited HANDOFF or NOT PRESSED control, a surface with no enumerable control, or a surface the probe cannot reach. The row's fix is the driven proof plus whatever it finds.

items.name: Fit
items.text: Nothing clipped, nothing overflowing, nothing under a modal; works at 1920 and 3840
items.instrument: tools/uxr3_fit_report.py (built in Part 2) over the shoot's frame records; the capture harness gains the records it reads in Part 2, before the shoot
items.pass_rule: ✓ iff the surface has an ok reading at 1920×1080, 3840×2160 and the user's 5120×1440, and none of the three frames records any of the following. (1) CLIPPED text: a RichTextLabel whose content is taller than its box, outside a ScrollContainer and without its own scrollbar (the harness's clipped_text); or a Label or Button whose text is cut, meaning one with clip_text on or a text_overrun_behavior other than no-trimming whose single-line text is wider than its content box, or an autowrapped Label showing fewer lines than it holds (truncated_text). (2) OVERFLOWING text or buttons: a text row or button outside the logical viewport, a scrolled list judged by its ScrollContainer's rect (buttons_offscreen, text_offscreen). (3) Anything UNDER A MODAL: a visible text row or button of the live frame (outside the map's SubViewport) whose centre lies inside the rect of a visible drawing Control (a Panel, PanelContainer, ColorRect, NinePatchRect or TextureRect that is not fully transparent) on a strictly higher CanvasLayer. The live frame is the layers at and above the topmost modal layer. A modal layer is one that holds a visible Control with a mouse filter other than IGNORE covering ≥ 95 % of the logical viewport; the content beneath a modal is suspended by it, by design, and is not read.

items.name: Discoverability
items.text: The surface's key action is reachable without the manual (the IQ-10 must_show line, re-read as a new player)
items.pass_rule: Each blind reader re-reads the surface's IQ-10 must_show line as a new player who has not read the manual, and marks ✓ iff the surface's key action (what the surface asks of the player, or the one thing it offers) is reachable from what the frame shows: a visible control, a stated key, or a named next step. A surface whose purpose is to inform passes when the way to leave it is visible. A reader who cannot judge from the evidence marks ✗ and says why. The mark is the one two of the three give.

scoring.mark: Every item of every surface is marked ✓ or ✗; none is skipped. An item a surface cannot evidence (no frame, no record) is ✗ and is filed with the gap as the row's first fix.
scoring.reader_marks: R2, R8 and R5's reader half come from three blind readers: Agent-tool subagents launched in one message. None sees another's marks. Each is given this file, the frames and the instrument and driven records, and is told nothing the records do not say. Each returns a mark and a cited frame per surface and reader-judged item, and may note R4 observations. The item's mark is the one two of the three give (tools/score_panel.py eyes's rule; here no reader may abstain). The spread is recorded as 3–0 or 2–1.
scoring.disagreement: The two-of-three mark stands. A 2–1 ✗ is filed like a 3–0 ✗, with the spread on the row.
scoring.score: A surface's score is its count of ✓, out of 8.
scoring.worst_five: The five lowest scores. A tie goes to the surface earlier in the review order, the one with more time on screen.
scoring.filing: Every ✗ becomes a docs/BUG_FIXES.md row in a new section '§UXR-3 — the review', with its frame(s), tagged ⟨SF step=pre-deploy S12 · UXR-3 <surface> · pillar=ui_ux⟩. The owner is S12 ('UXR-3 fixes'); the completion is the item re-read ✓ on that surface. ✗s of one item with one cause on several surfaces of one scene share a row that names every surface and its frame. Rows already owned (UXR-X9, UXR-X28) are cross-referenced, not re-filed. A crash or a P1 found while reading heads the list as a P1, owner S12.
scoring.no_fix: Nothing is fixed in S11, not even a one-liner, so the reading stays S12's clean baseline.
scoring.top_five: 'The top five by time on screen' are the first five groups below: the war room, the morning dispatch, the Generals screen, the diplomacy wizard with the settlement table, and the Strategic Ledger.
s11_done_when: every surface in the order has a reading (all eight items marked)
every ✗ is filed with owner S12
scoring.s12_done_when: §UXR-3's own done-when belongs to S12: every surface of the top five groups reads 8 of 8, and no surface reads under 6 of 8. S12 re-reads only the flipped items, against this file. Where the S11 reading already meets it on a surface, the review records that.
scoring.side_desk: UXR-D4, the Side Desk, does not exist at S11. It lands at S12b with its own census and is not scored here.
scoring.users_eyes: UXR-4 at S15: the user's own marks at 5120×1440 override the readers'.

evidence.tree: the committed master at this file's commit; every record names its client_commit
evidence.payloads: tools/iq10_capture_payloads.py, re-captured on that tree into the session's scratch directory (the mock parser, sandboxed saves; the player's 8005 never touched)
evidence.shoot: tools/iq10_run_captures.py --physical --physical-scale auto over the whole manifest at the five resolutions, Text size 100 %, HUD width Full, High contrast off; one engine at a time; the window parked off the desktop with OS input disabled; each frame's stray_input and focus are read before it is trusted
evidence.high_contrast_on: the same shoot with --high-contrast, recorded beside R3, never scored
evidence.reader_frames: each surface's 1920×1080 and 5120×1440 frames (a surface that does not fill the screen is cropped to its own top-level rects, never scaled); any of the five may be opened
evidence.action_probe: tools/uxr3_action_probe.py with tools/uxr3_action_probe.gd, built in Part 2 in the IQ-10 pattern: the same payloads, scenes, entry methods and steps, at 1920×1080 and the derived scale 1.0, with every API stubbed. In the live frame (R7's), every visible BaseButton, every visible Control showing the pointing-hand cursor and every BBCode [url] link of a visible RichTextLabel is a control. Each enabled control is pressed in a fresh instance of the surface: a button or pointing-hand control by a click at its centre as the player gives it (a synthetic press and release; where another control would take that click, the probe records what took it and presses the control by its own signal), a link by its label's meta_clicked. The frame is read before the press and again 2 frames and 500 ms (at least 30 frames) after it; what changes on its own over 500 ms with no press is read once per surface and set aside. The answer is VISIBLE when something on screen changed (see R6); HANDOFF when the only response is an API call the stub records or a signal the surface emits; SILENT when nothing at all happened. Controls that change the scene, quit, save, load or start a new game, and links to an outside address, are NOT PRESSED. Disabled controls are listed with their tooltip and the text beside them.
evidence.live_records: the Mode C session (tools/mode_c_driven_session.py: the real main.tscn against a sandboxed backend on an unused port; every screen key, typed orders, four end-turn roads, every modal answered) and the existing driven tests, each cited by name per surface
evidence.committed: the records under docs/audits/uxr3/ and every frame a row cites (force-added); the regenerable bulk stays out of git
